content:
Every task gets a description that states the requirement in full: what is wanted, why, the constraint that shapes it, and the files or endpoints involved. A bare title is a reminder, not a requirement - it loses exactly the implementation detail the task list exists to preserve.

As work proceeds, comment on the task with what is learned: the decision taken and its alternative, the trap found, the thing that turned out to be wrong. A task should read back as a complete account of its own implementation. Anything that outlives the task still also goes to a rule/decision/architecture memory.
summary: Every task gets a description that states the requirement in full: what is wanted, why, the constraint that shapes it,...
title: A task must carry enough detail to be implemented without the conversation

content:
When a platform supports a field, USE IT - do not settle for the local copy. Time spent is the one that was missed repeatedly: memory_task_start/stop/done record time entries locally, and none of it reached asoode, so every task on the board read 0 minutes while the local store held real work. asoode has POST /tasks/:id/spend-time {begin, end}; the interface must expose time tracking as a capability and the flusher must mirror it like any other mutation.

The general rule: if the local store records something and the provider can represent it, mirroring it is part of the feature, not an enhancement. Check the platform's DTOs for what is representable before deciding what to send.
summary: When a platform supports a field, USE IT - do not settle for the local copy
title: Mirror everything the provider can hold, time tracking included

content:
When this project is bound to an asoode work package, WORK ITS QUEUE - do not just report it.

The loop, one task at a time:
1. Read the bound board at session start. If tasks are waiting, take the highest-priority
   actionable one (state todo or in_progress). Do not ask which - pick and go.
2. Move it to in_progress on BOTH sides, and start time tracking.
3. Do the work. Record what comes up as it comes up: comments on the task, and anything
   that outlives it as a rule/decision/architecture memory.
4. Mark it done on both sides, stop the clock, then take the next one.

Do NOT auto-start a task whose state is blocked, blocker, paused, or cancelled, and stop to
ask when the work needs a decision only the user can make (an API choice, a product call, a
credential). Say which task you are on before starting it, so it can be redirected.

This deliberately OVERRIDES the default 'a queued task is a requirement, not an instruction'
contract for asoode-bound projects. That default still holds everywhere else: it protects the
capture case, where the user parks a requirement mid-session and does not want the session
derailed. Binding a project to an asoode board is the explicit opt-in to the loop.
summary: When this project is bound to an asoode work package, WORK ITS QUEUE - do not just report it
title: Work the bound asoode task queue autonomously, one task at a time

content:
Do not merge, rename away, delete or transfer tasks/memories between memory projects, and never link one project's boards to another. Project history is the asset this server exists to keep; mixing two projects corrupts both and is not recoverable from a snapshot, because the snapshot records the merged state as if it were true.

Duplicate registrations DO exist - the same repo registered twice under different slugs (see [[duplicate-memory-projects-in-this-workspace]]). The correct handling is to pick the project actually in use, act only on that one, and REPORT the duplicate for the user to retire. Never retire it yourself, and never 'tidy up' by consolidating.
summary: Do not merge, rename away, delete or transfer tasks/memories between memory projects, and never link one project's boards to another
title: Never merge, move or cross-link data between memory projects

content:
A task is the unit of work someone would pick up, review, or hand over. When part of one carries enough detail to be worked, argued about, or completed on its own, it should be a SUB-TASK (memory_task_add with parent_id, or memory_task_plan with parent_index) rather than a paragraph inside a description.

The test: could this part be assigned to someone else, or finished on a different day, without the parent being finished? Then it is a sub-task. Sub-tasks do not clutter the top-level list - it hides them the way a board does - so the cost of making one is near zero and the cost of burying real work in prose is that nobody sees it.

Still decompose by DELIVERABLE, not by step: 'write the test' is not a sub-task of 'add the endpoint', it is part of doing it.
summary: A task is the unit of work someone would pick up, review, or hand over
title: Decompose a task into sub-tasks when a part deserves its own record

content: After fixing any bug in this project, you must update the local installation so the running daemon reflects the fix. Rebuild the frontend if it changed (cd frontend && npm run build), then run `uv run memory-mcp-setup` to reinstall the runtime/UI and reload the launchd daemon, and verify the daemon is healthy. A bug fix is not considered complete until the local installation has been updated.
summary: After fixing any bug in this project, you must update the local installation so the running daemon reflects the fix
title: Update the local installation after every bug fix
